items.title: Warriors’ Steph Curry calls out Jimmy Butler for hilarious Instagram post
items.content:
Golden State Warriors star Jimmy Butler trolled Steph Curry in a recent series of pictures posted on Instagram.

Butler, who is on a trip to Amsterdam, posted pictures of his overseas workout — but with a twist. It appears Butler photoshopped Curry’s face over his own in each of the five photos.

Jimmy Butler played comedian during his trip to the Netherlands as he posted a hilarious series of photos of himself, only with Steph Curry’s face replacing his own. Instagram/jimmybutlerCurry commented on the Instagram post, “What is wrong with you” along with a laughing emoji. 

Butler has earned a reputation for his comedic demeanor off the court. In 2023 with the Miami Heat, Butler showed up to NBA Media Day with a bizarre hairstyle that later became known as “Emo Jimmy.” 

Steph Curry’s comment on Jimmy Butler’s IG:

“What is wrong with you ” pic.twitter.com/R9q6AQ2Bon

— aly ✶ (@jinthirty) August 7, 2026Jimmy Butler has earned a reputation for having a lighthearted, comedic demeanor off the court, which includes trolling his teammates.  Instagram/jimmybutlerThis also isn’t the first time Butler has involved Curry in one of his humorous antics as the Warriors duo previously pranked former teammate Buddy Hield.

Butler and Curry are obviously close enough to joke with one another, including the latter calling out the former for his hilarious Instagram post. 

While the Warriors are keeping things lighthearted off the court, the team has several question marks heading into the 2026-27 season.

Steph Curry will be tasked with handling the Warriors’ offensive load while Jimmy Butler recovers from a torn ACL.  NBAE via Getty ImagesAside from the LeBron James sweepstakes, Golden State was extremely quiet in free agency. Its most notable move of the offseason was selecting Yaxel Lendeborg as the No. 11 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.

As Butler and Moses Moody recover from injuries, the Warriors have once again placed the offensive load on Curry’s shoulders. While the 38-year-old remains an elite player, that is no easy task for a star who is hoping to get his squad a playoff spot.

items.title: Magic To Hire Mavs’ Josh Broghamer As Assistant Coach
items.content:
Although he was initially expected to stay on Dusty May‘s coaching staff with the Mavericks, Josh Broghamer will be leaving Dallas to join the Magic, reports Marc Stein of The Stein Line (via Twitter).

Both Mike Curtis of The Dallas Morning News and Grant Afseth of DallasSportsJournal.com have confirmed the news and report that Broghamer will be an assistant coach in Orlando.

Broghamer has been an assistant with Dallas for the past three seasons, largely focusing on player development. He was the Mavericks’ Summer League coach in 2025 and conducted Cooper Flagg‘s pre-game workouts throughout the 2025/26 campaign. Flagg, last year’s No. 1 overall pick, is the NBA’s reigning Rookie of the Year.

Broghamer will be reuniting with new Magic head coach Sean Sweeney, his former colleague in Dallas and Milwaukee, as well as veteran assistant coach Popeye Jones, who spent last season with the Mavs (it was technically his second stint as an assistant in Dallas).

According to the National Basketball Coaches Association, Broghamer got his NBA start in 2013 as a video intern in Phoenix, spent four seasons under Jason Kidd with the Bucks, and had a five-year run with the Cavaliers before joining Kidd’s staff in Dallas in 2023. The Mavericks parted ways with Kidd earlier this offseason when the new front office regime took over.

Veteran assistant coach Phil Handy is now the lone holdover from last season’s Mavericks staff, Curtis and Afseth note.
